external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A deployed sensor device installed at a customer site that publishes readings and polls for firmware updates.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway
external_entities.notes: The pre-shared key is per fleet, not per device, and has not been rotated since deployment.

external_entities.name: technician
external_entities.description: A field technician who services sensor nodes using a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state what authentication the console has, if any.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An operator who views telemetry dashboards from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: A customer associated with a sensor node and its telemetry data.
external_entities.source_excerpt: to find out which customer the node belongs to

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker running on GKE that accepts sensor readings and forwards them to Pub/Sub.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer that picks up readings from Pub/Sub and writes them into the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

processes.name: dashboard
processes.description: A dashboard used by fleet operators to view telemetry data over BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used to check a node's key and determine which customer it belongs to.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A Pub/Sub service carrying readings from the device gateway to the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery data store containing telemetry, site addresses, and occupancy patterns.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: firmware bucket
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket from which sensor nodes poll firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_stores.notes: The bucket is public read. The source does not state whether nodes verify a signature before installing an image.

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: A sensor node publishes readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up the device record to check the key and determine the customer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings onto Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write telemetry
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery

data_flows.name: poll firmware
data_flows.description: A sensor node polls the firmware bucket for a new image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_flows.notes: The source says the bucket is public read. It does not state whether the image is signature-checked before installation.

data_flows.name: service node
data_flows.description: A field technician services a sensor node over its local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state what authentication the console has, if any.

data_flows.name: view dashboard
data_flows.description: A fleet operator views telemetry dashboards.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

data_flows.name: read telemetry
data_flows.description: The dashboard reads telemetry data from BigQuery.

trust_boundaries.name: customer sites
trust_boundaries.description: Customer site locations where sensor nodes are installed and outside the system owner's physical control.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the telemetry normalizer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which fleet operators view dashboards.

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway presents a non-web interface because the text identifies it as an MQTT broker.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the device gateway as an MQTT broker.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry normalizer presents a non-web interface because it is described as a Python consumer.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a Python consumer that picks up readings from Pub/Sub.

assumptions.assumption: The dashboard presents a web interface because it is described as a dashboard for operators to view.
assumptions.basis: The source says fleet operators look at dashboards; dashboards are modeled as a user-facing interface.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry is confidential because it contains a pre-shared key and customer association data.
assumptions.basis: The source says the registry checks the key and determines which customer the node belongs to.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub is confidential because it carries sensor readings that are customer data.
assumptions.basis: The source says accepted readings are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and later states that the telemetry lake contents are customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is confidential because it contains site addresses and occupancy patterns identified as customer data.
assumptions.basis: The source says, 'The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.'

assumptions.assumption: The customer-sites boundary is a tenant boundary because the nodes are installed on customer sites outside the system owner's physical control.
assumptions.basis: The source says the nodes are installed on customer sites and are outside the organization's physical control.
